In [[algebraic geometry]], the '''theorem of the cube''' is a condition for a [[line bundle]] over a product of three [[complete variety|complete varieties]] to be trivial. It was first discovered in the context of [[linear equivalence]] by the [[Italian school of algebraic geometry|Italian school]] of algebraic geometry. The modern version of the theorem was first published by [[Serge Lang]],{{sfnp|Lang|1983}} who credited it to [[André Weil]].{{sfnp|Kleiman|2005}} A treatment by means of [[sheaf cohomology]], and description in terms of the [[Picard functor]], was given by [[David Mumford]].{{sfnp|Mumford|1970}}

==Statement==
The theorem states that for any [[complete variety|complete varieties]] <math>U</math>, <math>V</math> and <math>W</math> over an algebraically closed field, and given points <math>u</math>, <math>v</math> and <math>w</math> on them, any [[invertible sheaf]] <math>L</math> which has a trivial restriction to each of <math>U\times V\times\{w\}</math>, <math>U\times \{v\}\times W</math>, and <math>\{u\}\times V\times W</math> is itself trivial.{{sfnp|Mumford|1970|p=55|loc=the result there is slightly stronger in that one of the varieties need not be complete and can be replaced by a connected scheme}} 

===Special cases===
On a [[ringed space]] <math>X</math>, an invertible sheaf <math>L</math> is ''trivial'' if it is isomorphic to <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math> as an <math>\mathcal{O}_X</math>-module. If the base <math>X</math> is a [[complex manifold]], then an invertible sheaf is (the sheaf of sections of) a [[holomorphic line bundle]], and trivial means holomorphically equivalent to a [[trivial bundle]], not just topologically equivalent.

===Restatement using biextensions===
Weil's result has been restated in terms of [[biextension]]s, a concept now generally used in the [[duality theory of abelian varieties]].{{sfnp|Polishchuk|2003|p=122}}

==Theorem of the square==
The '''theorem of the square'''{{sfnp|Lang|1983}}{{sfnp|Mumford|1970|p=59}} is a corollary (also due to Weil) applying to an [[abelian variety]] <math>A</math>. One version of it states that the function <math>\phi_L</math> taking <math>x\in A</math> to <math>T_x^*L\otimes L^{-1}</math> is a group homomorphism from <math>A</math> to <math>\operatorname{Pic}(A)</math> (where <math>T_x^*</math> is translation by <math>x</math> on line bundles).
